story: How a team of young people helped rebuild healthcare.gov (2015)
text: I saw Mikey Dickerson talk about his experience in the initial recovery phase of healthcare.gov at Velocity in 2014. I think it shows just how insane the situation was. [VIDEO]

According to this talk, the work hours were pretty insane to fix healthcare.gov. From the 2014 Velocity Conference in New York City, Mikey Dickerson's keynote: "One Year After healthcare.gov: Where Are We Now? [VIDEO]

story: How Healthcare.gov Botched $600M Worth of Contracts
text: Part of the issue is everyone who is present at every meeting gets billed for the time at the meeting for the project. Mikey Dickerson talked about how there were ~50 contractor firms and nobody seemed to be in charge. This is good for all contractors because if nobody's in charge then nobody gets in trouble. [VIDEO]

story: Tech workers are increasingly looking to leave Silicon Valley
text: >How do you switch from one strain to another? End up around people that already have that strain, get their attention, and become friends so you can learn and they can teach. You unfortunately just can't teach yourself everything. It sounds like another form of pedigree selection. Or maybe dividing the field up into "us vs. them". Pretty understandable sentiment if you get pushed into fixing Healthcare.gov like he describes in one of his talks and working with guys arguing about tickets not existing because they're on different ticket systems and people with zero motivation to build a decent product. Wastage is immense in IT from the sounds of it in this talk: [VIDEO]
